newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Orthodox Bank has 219 mln lev loss in 96.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Orthodox Bank has 219 mln lev loss in 96.

text.p: Bulgaria's private St Nikola International Orthodox Bank (IOB) posted a 219.1 million lev loss for 1996, figures published in the State Gazette showed.

The bank's loss for last year adds to losses for previous years which total 448.5 million levs, the bank's balance sheet showed. Last year, the bank's income was 16.9 billion levs compared to spending of 17.1 billion levs.
At end-December, bank assets totalled 7.8 billion levs, of which around a third were loans to financial institutions, companies and individuals worth 2.6 billion levs.
Funds from financial institutions, companies and individuals stood at 6.2 billion levs at end-December.
Last month the IOB decided to raise its capital to 32.2 billion levs from 2.2 billion levs through a new share issue.
The bank said two Russian companies -- Yukos Petroleum through its Bulgarian branch, and Rossoil -- had become shareholders. Bank officials declined to elaborate on the size of the stakes.

The Orthodox Bank was set up some three years ago by the Bulgarian, Russian and Serbian Orthodox patriarchy, the Armenian Church, Private Agricultural and Investment Bank, and Touristsport bank, later renamed Trade and Savings Bank. Both banks have been declared bankrupt by the court. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 91188, 981 4145
